bib.title: CAPE: Encoding Relative Positions with Continuous Augmented Positional Embeddings
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2021 (35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can absolute sinusoidal positional embeddings be made to generalize to unseen input lengths and sizes like relative ones, without changing the attention mechanism?
hypothesis: Augmenting continuous absolute positions with random global shift, local shift and global scaling during training keeps relative-position information and gives better generalization than abspos, sinpos and (at lower cost) relpos.
contributions: new augmented continuous positional embedding (CAPE), which encodes some relative position information in a computationally efficient way, and improves generalization performance compared to other positional embeddings across a variety of domains: machine translation, image and speech recognition
a single vision Transformer (UniViT) trained with CAPE on the mix of different resolutions
new CAPE-based adaptive training scheme for ASR that eliminates need for padding

method.summary: CAPE uses continuous sinusoidal positions (tokens index for text, scaled [-1,1] coordinates for images, seconds for audio) and at training time applies mean-normalisation, a random global shift, per-token local shift and a global scale; at inference only mean-normalisation. It is compared with nopos, sinpos, learnable abspos and learnable relpos in ViT/DeiT-B image classification, CTC speech recognition and ADMIN WMT'14 translation.
method.task: image classification (ImageNet), CTC ASR (WSJ, TED-LIUM v3), machine translation (WMT'14 En-De, En-Fr)

datasets.name: ImageNet (+ ImageNet-v2 a,b,c test sets)
datasets.split: train on ImageNet; top-1/top-5 on validation and ImageNet-v2-{a,b,c}
datasets.preprocessing: eval images resized to 160, 224, 384, 672 px; ViT training follows DeiT (Touvron 2020): Rand-Augment, Mixup, Cutmix, random erasing, repeated augmentation

datasets.name: WSJ
datasets.split: si284 train, nov93dev valid, nov92 test
datasets.preprocessing: punctuation tokens removed from si284 transcripts; Kaldi recipe

datasets.name: TED-LIUM v3
datasets.split: v3 train; valid/test consistent with earlier releases

datasets.name: Robust Video (RV)
datasets.split: clean and noisy test sets; also 8 re-segmented sets of 10-45s
datasets.source: in-house English video dataset from public social media videos, de-identified

datasets.name: WMT'14 En-De
datasets.split: newstest2013 valid, newstest2014 test; 32K subword vocab
datasets.preprocessing: ADMIN recipe; for long-sentence eval, test sentences stacked to 300+ target tokens (3k pairs -> 270 pairs)

datasets.name: WMT'14 En-Fr
datasets.split: provided valid file; newstest14 test; 40k subword vocab

other.positional variants: nopos, abspos (learnable), sinpos (Eq 3-4), CAPE (Delta_max=0.5, eps_max=1/N, lambda_max=1.4)

models.name: UniViT (ViT-B; also -S, -Ti sizes for throughput)
models.architecture: ViT with CAPE trained on mixed resolutions
models.context: batch resized to random size in [128,320]^2 step 32

models.name: CTC acoustic model
models.architecture: 1D conv (kernel 7, stride 3) + GLU + 36 Transformer layers, 4 heads, then linear; letters (26) + apostrophe + word boundary tokens

other.relpos context: 26.8s left/right in Sec 5.2 (27.6s in figure legend and Appendix C.4)

other.CAPE: global shift 5/10/50, local shift 0.5, no global scaling, no mean-normalisation, BOS prepended to source, source positions scaled by alpha=1.0337 DE / 1.1632 FR

training.objective: cross-entropy (ViT); CTC (ASR; seq2seq cross-entropy in an ablation); ADMIN MT recipe
training.optimizer: AdamW (ViT); Adagrad (ASR); MT: ADMIN/fairseq recipe, not restated
training.batch_size: ViT 64 per GPU on 16 GPUs (384^2: 32 per GPU on 32 GPUs); ASR dynamic batching, average 240s/GPU
training.dropout: ASR conv dropout 0.3; Transformer dropout and layer drop 0.4 WSJ, 0.1 TED-LIUM v3
training.regularisation: ViT: Rand-Augment, Mixup, Cutmix, random erasing, repeated augmentation; ASR: SpecAugment (2 freq masks, 10 time masks, p=0.1, max 30 freq bands, max 50 frames, no time warping), layer drop
training.hardware: ViT/UniViT 16x V100 32GB (32 GPUs at 384^2); ASR 16x V100 32GB; MT DE 4x V100 16GB, FR 8x V100 16GB
training.wall_clock: ViT 19-56h, UniViT 37h; ASR 1 day WSJ, 3-4 days TED-LIUM v3; MT DE 30h (6L-6L) / 70h (18L-18L), FR 60h
training.seeds: MT: 3 random seeds per configuration (3 runs avg.)

other.framework: Flashlight (ViT, ASR); Fairseq via ADMIN code (MT)

inference.decoding: ASR: greedy acoustic model, no language model; MT: beam 4 DE, 5 FR
inference.samples: MT 3 runs averaged; ViT/ASR single run (not stated)

parameters.TTA resolutions: r, r-32, r+32 with logits averaged, r=224 or 384

metrics.name: Top-1 / Top-5 accuracy
metrics.definition: ImageNet val and ImageNet-v2-a/b/c at 160/224/384/672 px

metrics.name: WER
metrics.definition: no LM; by duration bin <10, 10-15, 15-20, >=20s and total; RV re-segmented to 10-45s

metrics.name: per-position log loss
metrics.definition: negative log loss across positions on stacked-sentence test sets

metrics.name: throughput
metrics.definition: images/s on a single 16GB V100, largest batch, average over 30 runs

eval.protocol: MT mean +- std over 3 runs; best checkpoint by valid BLEU; ASR and ViT results shown in figures with no stated seeds or confidence intervals.

availability.code: Appendix A gives a Python reference implementation; Fairseq/ADMIN and Flashlight code used; no CAPE repo link in text
availability.data: ImageNet, WSJ, TED-LIUM, LibriSpeech, WMT'14 public; RV in-house

results.claim: ViT-B trained at 224^2 with CAPE keeps higher ImageNet top-1 at 672^2 than abspos or sinpos.
results.setup: ViT-B/DeiT-B, ImageNet validation, trained 224^2, evaluated at 672^2 (bicubic-interpolated abspos)
results.table: Table 3, rows CAPE / abspos / sinpos (train 224^2), column ImageNet 672^2
results.note: Pdf text order of the CAPE row is hard to verify; 73.43, 72.21, 70.71 occur in Table 3 text.

results.claim: At 672^2 and 160^2 CAPE outperforms abspos by up to 25% and 2%.
results.quote: CAPE performs best, notably outperforming abspos on high (6722) and low (1602) resolutions up to 25% and 2%, respectively
results.note: Unit (relative or points) not stated; for the 224^2-trained model Table 3 gap at 672^2 is 1.2 points.

results.claim: UniViT with CAPE plus per-bin optimal resizing reaches 82.92% top-1.
results.setup: UniViT CAPE, ImageNet val split into 8 size bins, best resize strategy chosen per bin (selected on the validation set itself)
results.quote: By selecting an optimal resizing strategy in each bin we are able to improve top-1 accuracy to 82.92% (in comparison, the model has 81.26% on 2242 and 82.55% on 3842).

results.claim: Resizing test-time augmentation gives a 0.2-0.5% top-1 boost for sinpos and CAPE models.
results.setup: logits averaged over r, r-32, r+32, r=224 or 384
results.quote: get 0.2%-0.5% top-1 accuracy boost with this test time augmentation

results.claim: UniViT training takes only 1.1x the time of ViT at 224^2.
results.quote: UniViT training time is only 1.1x longer than ViT

results.claim: WMT'14 En-De 6L-6L: CAPE (Delta=5) test BLEU is within noise of relpos and above abspos and sinpos.
results.table: Table 2, rows 6L-6L DE CAPE Delta=5 / relpos / sinpos / abspos, column Test BLEU

results.claim: WMT'14 En-Fr 6L-6L: CAPE (Delta=5) beats relpos on test BLEU.
results.table: Table 2, FR 6L-6L, CAPE Delta=5 vs relpos, column Test BLEU

results.claim: On stacked long test sentences, relpos beats absolute embeddings beyond training lengths; CAPE generalizes better than abspos and sinpos, and similar to relpos on FR.
results.setup: 6L-6L DE and FR, stacked test sets of 300+ target tokens (Fig 8)
results.quote: for positions not seen during training (>200) relpos outperforms others. However, CAPE generalizes better than abspos and sinpos and, moreover, is able to generalize similar to relpos with more data (FR).

results.claim: A nopos TED-LIUM model is competitive with positional models on public data, but needs CTC loss, capacity and enough data; nopos WSJ model gets 45-50% WER.
results.setup: CTC AM trained on WSJ (81.5h) with nopos, in-domain data
results.quote: performs poorly having 45-50% WER even on in-domain data

results.claim: On TED-LIUM, CAPE or SpecAugment each cut WER by 4-5% vs. no augmentation; combined a further 2.5-3.5%.
results.quote: Including either CAPE or SpecAugment decreases the WER signiﬁcantly by 4-5%

results.claim: Learnable relative positional embeddings cost 1.1-3.3x forward/backward time in a Transformer layer vs none.
results.setup: V100 32GB, batch 50, emb 768, 8 heads, relpos context 1000 left/right, FP16, length 100 (max in table)
results.table: Table 9, top block, row Transformer layer, column FP16 Len-100

limits: CAPE applies only to attention-based models, and no testing was performed outside described modalities (Limitations).
A model must learn relative positioning; relative embeddings should help with small data (Limitations).
UniViT tested only for image recognition (Limitations).
No language-model pretraining tested; text experiments are only MT with ADMIN.
ASR and ViT results are mostly plots with no stated seeds or intervals; the best-resolution bin selection for 82.92% was chosen on validation data.
CAPE for MT needs source/target position scaling and a BOS token, with no mean-normalisation.
Relpos is better beyond training lengths on MT (DE).

terms.definition: continuous augmented positional embedding: continuous sinusoidal absolute positions with random global shift, local shift and global scaling at training time
a single vision Transformer trained with CAPE on a mix of image resolutions

lineage.note: improves absolute sinusoidal embedding (Vaswani et al.)
closest idea: discrete global position shifts; CAPE uses continuous shifts, scaling, local shifts
